source.title: Codebook Features: Sparse and Discrete Interpretability for Neural Networks
source.authors: Alex Tamkin; Mohammad Taufeeque; Noah D. Goodman

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures feature identification in codebook-trained networks and compares code classifiers with neuron classifiers. This is a different method from the original toy-model geometry experiments; it does not test the original networks’ feature-direction geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper reports code purity and code-versus-neuron classifier results. Its FSM codebook experiments are relevant to superposition broadly, but use a codebook bottleneck introduced during training and do not measure the overlapping, nearly orthogonal direction geometry or sparsity-dependent transitions in V1. Topic-steering and language-model performance results do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes codebook features, a vector-quantization bottleneck added during finetuning. It uses superposition as its motivation and reports how well its own method performs: code purity, codes versus best-neuron classifiers, steering and LM loss. The neuron baseline sits inside the codebook-finetuned network, not the unmodified model, so the comparison measures the method, not how often or how strongly ordinary models show superposition. It does not measure feature geometry, sparsity transitions, capacity allocation, SAE features or feature dimensionality. Classed T4, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that codebook finetuning yields sparse, discrete, often interpretable codes with modest performance loss, and that the codes can causally steer behaviour. They also claim codebooks 'overcome' or 'mitigate' the superposition problem in the FSM setting by representing more features than neurons. They note that the method modifies the network and that many codes in larger models lack clear interpretations.
record.recipe_differences: The study finetunes networks with vector-quantization codebook bottlenecks and measures code purity and classifier performance; it does not reproduce the original toy-model setup or measure feature-direction angles and sparsity transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Code purity is higher in the first MLP layer and declines in higher layers. Performance also varies with codebook placement and k, but those model-performance results do not directly measure the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In codebook-finetuned networks (TokFSM 4-layer; Pythia-410M on WikiText-103), single neurons are worse classifiers than codes of states or regex features at matched recall. The FSM network has 128-dim MLP layers but represents 100 states and 686 state-plus-digit features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A discrete codebook bottleneck yields units that classify known features more precisely than any single neuron of the same finetuned network.

fits_no_version.finding: In the TokFSM codebook model, code purity is very high at the first MLP layer and declines in later layers. States that share a code have similar next-token distributions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In codebook-bottlenecked networks, codes become less state-pure in deeper layers as states with similar predictions are merged.

record.problems: The LLM feature-classification experiment is described as preliminary; regular expressions are imperfect proxies, and codes were selected for interpretable patterns, potentially biasing the comparison. The study finetunes the base models with codebook bottlenecks. Figure 8 does not state exact purity values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results bearing on the claim versions were omitted. Model language-model accuracy, topic steering, and inference-speed results were left out because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy-model geometry, near-orthogonality or sparsity-dependent transition is measured.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation of dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.
No measurement in an unmodified LLM. Neuron baselines are taken inside codebook-finetuned networks, and no SAE is used.
SAE features are not studied. Dictionary learning is discussed conceptually only (Appendix F).
Features-as-directions versus features-as-points is argued conceptually (Appendix F.1), not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked r1 to V4 and labelled it 'supports'; that label is removed. r1 compares the method with neurons of an already-modified network, and the authors flag selection bias in which codes were tested. The paper's superposition statements are interpretations of its own method's success, not measurements of superposition in standard models.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test whether ordinary toy networks store sparse features as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, or whether their geometry changes with feature sparsity.
No test of capacity competition allocating dedicated dimensions to important features and shared dimensions to others.
No test of non-capacity mechanisms causing polysemantic neurons.

The LLM experiment compares code and neuron classifiers in a codebook-finetuned WikiText-103 model; it does not test SAE recovery or establish that the same feature distribution holds in the unmodified base model.
The study does not test SAE features or whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The paper discusses directions versus points conceptually but does not test whether superposed features in ordinary networks are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.note: The authors describe the experiment as preliminary. Regular expressions are imperfect feature proxies, and selecting codes for interpretable patterns may bias results in favor of code classifiers.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (codes) with a neuron baseline in the codebook-finetuned 410M model. It is not a measurement of features spread across neurons in an unmodified LLM, and no SAE is involved. The authors call it preliminary: codes were selected for interpretability and regexes are imperfect proxies. It should not be linked to V4.

relation.reason: Superposition motivates the codebook method; the reported comparisons evaluate that method rather than independently measuring a claim version.

tranche.reason: The results evaluate an introduced vector-quantization bottleneck: code purity, classification, steering and language-model performance. They measure the method's performance after modifying the network, rather than directly testing V1–V6.

source_check.notes: All ten rows describe method performance and appropriately have no linked claim version. Appendix E.7 itself reports searching 410 million neurons; this wording appears to conflate neuron count with the model's parameter count.
